Interpret maps using the map keys and other features
Describe location using latitude and longitude
At the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

A map is a visual representation of an earth's surface or specific part of it. It shows the exact location of places, their sizes and distances. Maps differ in layout but usually share the given features on the right.
* Source: Here, you can document your source of the map if available.
Can you think of a phrase to help you remember the order of cardinal directions?
Used to describe the direction of a location in relation to the other locations around it.
The vertical imaginary lines that tell the location east or west of the Prime Meridian.
The horizontal imaginary lines that tell the location north or south of the Equator.
Both latitude and longitude are measured in degrees(°).

The compass needle
always points to the magnetic north.
The letters indicate the cardinal directions.
The bearing tells how many degrees away from the north or south. Traveling north means 0° bearing.
A compass is a device used in navigation.
To travel from the lighthouse to the lake you would need to move directly South, as shown by the arrow on the map.
You would need to move South.
To travel from the lake to the mountains, you would need to move Northeast - upward and toward the right, as shown by the arrow on the map.
You would need to move Northeast.

To travel from the mountains to the treasure while avoiding boggy terrain, you would need to travel southwest through the forest and once through, change your direction to southeast, as depicted by the two arrows on the map.
Lines of latitude are horizontal imaginary lines that tell us our location north or south of the Equator.
Lines of longitude are vertical imaginary lines that tell us our location east or west of the Prime Meridian.
All statements are correct. Jodhpur is to the west of Kanpur, Delhi is located in the north, and Kolkata is to the southeast of Delhi.
Use the compass to know which direction you are facing: Hold it flat on the palm of your hand, and align the needle's magnetic arrow to the cardinal direction North.
Use the cardinal directions, latitude and longitude to determine your exact location on a map.
When using a map, place it on a flat surface and place the compass on the map.
